news.title: Inside new Morocco’s Mohammed VI Football Complex hosting the 2026 U-17 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: Four pitches, a centralised tournament format and a growing commitment to women’s football place Rabat at the heart of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. When the world’s emerging female football stars arrive in Morocco for the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, they will compete for more than a trophy. They will step into a unique football environment designed to bring the game closer to supporters, create a showcase for young talent and underline Morocco’s growing ambitions as an international sporting destination. At the centre of that vision is Rabat’s Mohammed VI Football Complex, which will host matches from the opening round through the semi-finals across four pitches.

news.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Predicted Top 10
news.lede: The prestigious 2026 Ballon d’Or will be awarded on the 26th of October. Its winner is set to join the best of the best players to have won the award. Several players are actively making a case for themselves, signaling to the voters and the public that they deserve the honor. An evaluation of the statistics for all the male nominees of the Ballon d’Or allows for a direct comparison.

news.title: FIFA picks US as host of first Women’s Club World Cup in 2028
news.lede: ZURICH (AP) — The United States will host the inaugural FIFA Women’s Club World Cup in 2028, football’s governing body said Thursday. FIFA said the tournament featuring 19 of the best women’s clubs from around the world will take place January 5–30 in 2028, but did not announce host cities. The Women’s Club World Cup will be staged every four years after that. Seven clubs have already qualified for the inaugural event, FIFA said.

news.title: Teen prodigy’s World Cup dream revived as Sydney FC move aside
news.lede: Akol Akon’s hopes of playing at the under-17s FIFA World Cup have been revived as Sydney FC and Football Australia came to an agreement on his availability. It was reported by a number of outlets on Wednesday the winger would not represent Australia next month as the Sky Blues had blocked him from doing so. Akol Akon is the youngest player to ever feature in an A-League grand final. Sydney FC’s decision was reportedly related to concerns about the squad’s depth as well as Akon’s position in cementing himself as a key figure in the senior team.

news.title: Inaugural Fifa tournament confirmed with USA to host major football competition just months after World Cup
news.lede: THE USA has been confirmed as the host of the inaugural Women’s Club World Cup – and seven clubs have already qualified. The tournament will take place in January 2028 with 19 teams competing. Fifa announced the decision to stage the first edition in the United States on Thursday. The host cities and stadiums are yet to be confirmed, but Dame Sarai Bareman, Chief Women’s Football Officer at Fifa, claimed the nation was the best option.

news.title: FIFA launches bidding war for 2030 and 2034 World Cup media rights in the United States
news.lede: FIFA has officially opened the bidding process for the United States television and streaming rights for the historic 2030 World Cup. World football's governing body is actively seeking innovative broadcasting approaches following a massive surge in American viewership during recent international tournaments. FIFA has officially launched an invitation to tender for the media broadcast rights to the 2030 World Cup. The available broadcasting packages cover extensive television and streaming coverage across both the United States and Puerto Rico.

news.title: FIFA increases 2027 Women’s World Cup preparation funding to $2.5m per team
news.lede: FIFA has approved a new financial package for the 2027 Women’s World Cup, raising preparation funding to $2.5m (£1.9m) for each participating national football association ahead of the tournament in Brazil. The decision was taken by the Bureau of the FIFA Council following a council meeting in Zurich, Switzerland, on 15 October 2026. The revised distribution model will include prize money, preparation funds and payments through the FIFA Club Benefits Programme, while players at the women’s tournament will receive the same level of services provided to their male counterparts at the 2026 Men’s World Cup. FIFA also confirmed that any surplus generated by the competition will be shared among participating member associations, with a designated portion set aside for players.
